rubrics.justification: Accurately interprets the provided Gardner 3BA features and gives a plausible description of expanded blastocyst, thinned zona, B-grade ICM, and A-grade TE. Slight overreach in claiming fine details like visible nuclei/tight junctions from a single image.
Strong integration of age, tubal factor diagnosis, ovarian reserve, BMI, sperm quality, endometrial thickness, first-cycle status, and smoking with embryo quality and prognosis.

Overall logical and well-structured, with a clear link from embryo grade and patient factors to prognosis. Minor issues include somewhat confident quantitative adjustments for smoking and overstatement that TE is the strongest predictor in all contexts.

Generally consistent with IVF practice: eSET in a good-prognosis young patient, no ERA after first failure, limited role for PGT-A, and attention to hydrosalpinx. Small deviations include suggesting nicotine replacement/very short-term cessation effects and some overly specific unsupported probability modifiers.
Provides clear next steps for transfer, luteal support, smoking cessation, exercise modification, and future-cycle contingencies, with practical and case-specific recommendations.
